PriorUnitAssumption: Displayed MHz for a direct core offset or clock target; displayed tool unit for memory; displayed percent for power.

DefaultStartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The automatic tier value is a bounded starting experiment, not a calibrated stable maximum.

NVIDIA-Ampere.Label: NVIDIA Ampere (RTX 30)
NVIDIA-Ampere.Strategy: Use a small core step first; power, transient load, and GDDR6X memory-junction heat often dominate sustained behavior.
Caveats: High-end Ampere cards may receive little sustained benefit from a core offset.
Check memory-junction temperature before memory escalation on GDDR6X cards.

NVIDIA-Ampere-Entry.Label: NVIDIA Ampere entry (RTX 3060 / 3060 Ti)
NVIDIA-Ampere-Entry.Strategy: Use a practical GDDR6 entry-tier core start, then test memory separately.
Caveats: The 3060 and 3060 Ti have different memory buses and sample behavior.
Do not copy one sample's maximum memory offset.

StartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The tier combines different RTX 3060 and RTX 3060 Ti samples; use the exact-model evidence below when available.

ModelStartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The +100 MHz tier start is 143% of the cited RTX 3060 Ti FE +70 MHz sample. Keep it only as an active usable starting experiment, not a conservative estimate.

NVIDIA-Ampere-Mainstream.Label: NVIDIA Ampere mainstream (RTX 3070 / 3070 Ti)
NVIDIA-Ampere-Mainstream.Strategy: Use the mainstream Ampere start; power-limit exposure varies materially by board.
Caveats: 3070 and 3070 Ti have different memory and power paths.
Verify board-specific power behavior before raising limits.

NVIDIA-Ampere-High.Label: NVIDIA Ampere high tier (RTX 3080)
NVIDIA-Ampere-High.Strategy: Use an active but bounded core start because core headroom can be limited and GDDR6X performance can degrade before artifacts.
Caveats: Memory error replay can reduce performance without an immediate crash.
Require memory-junction and power-path evidence.

StartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The +50 MHz start is 83% of the cited RTX 3080 FE +60 MHz sample. It is a practical active start, not a conservative one.

NVIDIA-Ampere-UpperHigh.Label: NVIDIA Ampere upper-high tier (RTX 3080 Ti)
NVIDIA-Ampere-UpperHigh.Strategy: Use a moderate core start and keep GDDR6X memory as a separately validated round.
Caveats: Power-target exposure varies substantially across boards.
Do not transfer the highest reviewed core offset.

NVIDIA-Ampere-Flagship.Label: NVIDIA Ampere flagship (RTX 3090)
NVIDIA-Ampere-Flagship.Strategy: Use a conservative flagship start; GDDR6X thermal and power behavior dominate.
Caveats: Memory performance can fall before a visible crash.
Require sustained memory-temperature monitoring.

NVIDIA-Ampere-FlagshipTi.Label: NVIDIA Ampere flagship Ti (RTX 3090 Ti)
NVIDIA-Ampere-FlagshipTi.Strategy: Use an active start only after acknowledging how little power and thermal headroom the RTX 3090 Ti may expose.
Caveats: Some boards do not expose additional power-limit headroom.
Use sustained power and memory-temperature guards.

StartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The +75 MHz start is 68% of the cited +110 MHz high sample and equals the lower +75 MHz sample. It is an active start, not a conservative guarantee.

NVIDIA-Ada.Label: NVIDIA Ada (RTX 40)
NVIDIA-Ada.Strategy: Core then memory is a useful experiment order; reduced-power or curve tuning can be competitive on efficient cards.
Caveats: Keep high-end connector and power-path evidence in scope.
Do not transfer Afterburner-style values to a different tool without checking its unit.

NVIDIA-Ada-Entry.Label: NVIDIA Ada entry (RTX 4060 / 4060 Ti)
NVIDIA-Ada-Entry.Strategy: Use a practical core-first start; verify the specific 4060 or 4060 Ti board instead of copying the best review sample.
Caveats: The 4060 Ti 8 GB and 16 GB remain separate configurations.
Do not infer core headroom from memory capacity.

NVIDIA-Ada-Mainstream.Label: NVIDIA Ada mainstream (RTX 4070 / 4070 Super)
NVIDIA-Ada-Mainstream.Strategy: Use the mainstream Ada starting tier, then retain only measured benefits above noise.
Caveats: Core and memory values from review tables use different units.
Power and cooling differ by board.

NVIDIA-Ada-UpperMid.Label: NVIDIA Ada upper-mid (RTX 4070 Ti / 4070 Ti Super)
NVIDIA-Ada-UpperMid.Strategy: Use a larger one-step core start than 4070 while preserving one-variable testing.
Caveats: 4070 Ti and 4070 Ti Super are distinct SKUs.
Board power and cooling determine whether extra headroom is useful.

NVIDIA-Ada-High.Label: NVIDIA Ada high tier (RTX 4080 / 4080 Super)
NVIDIA-Ada-High.Strategy: Use a practical high-tier core start and require connector, PSU, and sustained thermal evidence for power experiments.
Caveats: Power-limit exposure varies significantly across custom cards.
Do not copy a maximum average clock as a slider offset.

StartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The tier default is 95% of the cited RTX 4080 Super +185 MHz sample. It is an active start, not a conservative one.

ModelStartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: The +175 MHz start is 85% of the cited RTX 4080 FE +205 MHz sample. It is an active start, not a conservative one.

NVIDIA-Ada-Flagship.Label: NVIDIA Ada flagship (RTX 4090)
NVIDIA-Ada-Flagship.Strategy: Start the simple-offset path more conservatively because the RTX 4090's power path is the controlling risk.
Caveats: Require dedicated 16-pin connector and power-path checks.
Prefer a curve or reduced-power route where appropriate.

NVIDIA-Blackwell.Label: NVIDIA Blackwell (RTX 50)
NVIDIA-Blackwell.Strategy: Validate the exact SKU and driver behavior first; power and thermal headroom are not implied by the newer generation.
Caveats: Desktop RTX 5090 has a separate coordinated curve/power reference route.
Newer tools and drivers may display different units or apply clamping.

NVIDIA-Blackwell-Entry.Label: NVIDIA Blackwell entry (RTX 5060 / 5060 Ti)
NVIDIA-Blackwell-Entry.Strategy: Start below the mainstream Blackwell tier; core first, memory separately, and stock power by default.
Caveats: Do not transfer RTX 5070/5080/5090 power or curve assumptions.
The 8 GB and 16 GB 5060 Ti variants remain separate hardware configurations.

NVIDIA-Blackwell-Mainstream.Label: NVIDIA Blackwell mainstream (RTX 5070 / 5070 Ti)
NVIDIA-Blackwell-Mainstream.Strategy: Use the mainstream Blackwell starting tier; verify the actual board power ceiling before any power experiment.
Caveats: Board power headroom varies substantially among non-reference designs.
Keep memory as a separate round and respect Blackwell request clamping.

NVIDIA-Blackwell-High.Label: NVIDIA Blackwell high tier (RTX 5080)
NVIDIA-Blackwell-High.Strategy: Use a bounded core start and require connector, PSU, and sustained thermal evidence before power-ceiling work.
Caveats: Custom cards can expose much higher power ceilings than the reference design.
A higher exposed ceiling is not evidence of sufficient cooling or cabling.

StartEvidence.StartEvidenceNote: No normalized second-source RTX 5080 core-offset table was retained. The +200 MHz value is a single-source tier-level candidate with very-low prior confidence.

NVIDIA-Blackwell-Flagship.Label: NVIDIA Blackwell flagship (RTX 5090)
NVIDIA-Blackwell-Flagship.Strategy: Prefer the dedicated reduced-power/curve reference for RTX 5090; a simple-offset path starts more conservatively.
Caveats: High board power makes connector and sustained power-path evidence controlling.
Do not transfer the RTX 5090 profile to other Blackwell cards.

NVIDIA-Turing.Label: NVIDIA Turing (RTX 20 / GTX 16)
NVIDIA-Turing.Strategy: Use small core steps and keep memory as a separate experiment.
Caveats: Older firmware and tool support can vary by board.

NVIDIA-Pascal.Label: NVIDIA Pascal (GTX 10)
NVIDIA-Pascal.Strategy: Treat the card conservatively and prioritize cooling and driver-supported controls.
Caveats: Modern tuning-tool compatibility is not guaranteed.

NVIDIA-Generic.Label: NVIDIA generic
NVIDIA-Generic.Strategy: Use a reduced generic core-first ladder because generation-specific calibration is unavailable.
Caveats: Record the exact GPU model before treating the result as family-specific.

AMD-RDNA1.Label: AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000)
AMD-RDNA1.Strategy: Use one supported Adrenalin clock or offset step and treat memory separately.
Caveats: Confirm whether Adrenalin exposes an offset, actual clock, or profile.

AMD-RDNA2.Label: AMD RDNA2 (RX 6000)
AMD-RDNA2.Strategy: Efficiency and undervolt tuning are often competitive; memory-clock stability must be tested separately.
Caveats: Watch hotspot and per-model firmware limits.
Do not convert NVIDIA memory offsets to AMD clock targets.

AMD-RDNA3.Label: AMD RDNA3 (RX 7000)
AMD-RDNA3.Strategy: Review core clock target, power, and hotspot together before testing memory.
Caveats: Shared power and hotspot pressure can erase nominal clock gains.
Use the exact labels exposed by the installed Adrenalin version.

AMD-RDNA4.Label: AMD RDNA4 (RX 9000)
AMD-RDNA4.Strategy: Start conservatively with supported per-game profiles and current official controls.
Caveats: Do not assume RDNA3 values transfer to RDNA4.
Model-specific firmware behavior may be newer and less documented.

AMD-Generic.Label: AMD generic
AMD-Generic.Strategy: Use a reduced generic control step because generation-specific calibration is unavailable and Adrenalin units can differ.
Caveats: Generation-specific calibration is unavailable.

Intel-Alchemist.Label: Intel Arc Alchemist
Intel-Alchemist.Strategy: Use only controls exposed by the installed Intel Graphics Software and keep one variable under test.
Caveats: Desktop-style NVIDIA and AMD settings are not transferable.

Intel-Battlemage.Label: Intel Arc Battlemage
Intel-Battlemage.Strategy: Use a conservative one-variable test with official Intel controls.
Caveats: Driver and model support vary; do not assume an Alchemist profile transfers.

Intel-Generic.Label: Intel generic
Intel-Generic.Strategy: Use a reduced conservative one-variable test with official Intel controls.
Caveats: Generation-specific calibration is unavailable.
